q: Which method of metal connection uses metal pins that are deformed to create a permanent joint?
n: Riveting involves using metal pins (rivets) that are deformed at both ends to form a permanent joint. it is commonly used in steel structures and historical bridges. In contrast, bolting allows for easy disassembly, welding fuses materials together, and clamping is a temporary connection. Riveting joins plates with metal pins whose ends are hammered or deformed into a head. The joint is permanent. Source: Allen & Iano, Fundamentals of Building Construction, Ch. 11; AISC Steel Construction Manual (historical riveted connections).

q: What property of steel is primarily increased when the metal undergoes tempering?
n: Tempering reheats hardened steel below its critical temperature. This relieves internal stress and increases toughness, at some cost to hardness. Source: Callister, Materials Science and Engineering (Heat Treatment of Steels – Tempering).

q: What type of structural steel is coated with a layer of zinc to prevent corrosion?
n: Galvanized steel has a zinc coating, applied by hot-dipping or electroplating, to protect it from corrosion. Source: ASTM A123 (Hot-Dip Galvanizing); Callister, Materials Science and Engineering (Corrosion Prevention).

q: Which spraying technique is commonly used in construction for applying coatings with minimal overspray and high transfer efficiency, making it ideal for fine finishing and detailed work?
n: HVLP (High Volume Low Pressure) spraying uses a high volume of air at low pressure to atomize coatings, resulting in minimal overspray and high transfer efficiency. It is ideal for fine finishing and applications requiring precision. In contrast, airless spraying uses high pressure to atomize, electrostatic spraying utilizes electrical charge, and conventional spraying uses high pressure, leading to more overspray. HVLP (high volume, low pressure) spraying atomizes coating at low pressure. That means little overspray and high transfer efficiency, well suited to fine finishing. Source: US EPA and air-quality transfer-efficiency rules; PDCA Painting Standards (Spray Application).

q: Why is chlorine added to rubber paint, making it marketed as "chlorinated rubber paint"?
o: To increase flexibility in low temperatures
To enhance chemical and water resistance
n: Chlorine is added to rubber paint to increase its resistance to chemicals, water, and weathering, making it suitable for harsh environments like swimming pools, marine applications, and industrial surfaces. Chlorinated rubber paint forms a durable, impermeable film that withstands exposure to water and chemicals. It does not significantly improve flexibility, insulation, or drying time. Chlorinating natural rubber gives a film with excellent resistance to water and chemicals. It is used on pools, marine and industrial surfaces. Source: SSPC Painting Manual, Vol. 2 (Chlorinated Rubber Coatings); ASTM D16.

q: What is the typical vehicle type used in automotive lacquer to create a durable and glossy finish on surfaces?
n: Automotive lacquer typically uses nitrocellulose as the vehicle type, which forms a durable, glossy finish when applied to car surfaces. Nitrocellulose lacquers dry quickly and can be polished to a high shine. In contrast, epoxy resin is used for industrial coatings, polyurethane for durable finishes, and acrylic resin for water-based paints. Traditional automotive lacquers use nitrocellulose as the vehicle. They dry fast by solvent evaporation to a hard, glossy film. Source: ASTM D16 (Lacquer); Wicks et al., Organic Coatings: Science and Technology.

q: Why do galvanized surfaces that are at least 6 months old typically not require etching before paint application?
o: The surface has already become roough and porous
The surface becomes hydrophobic and repels paint
The galvanized surface becomes chemically inert
n: After about 6 months of exposure, galvanized surfaces undergo natural weathering, forming a rough and porous zinc patina that improves paint adhesion. This eliminates the need for additional etching. The zine coating does not deteriorate completely, and the surface does not become hydrophobic or chemically inert. Instead, it develops a slightly roughened texture ideal for coating. This is why newly galvanized surfaced need to be ethed before painting because the zinc coating is still making the surface smooth and oil, which affects paint adhesion. Galvanizing weathered for about 6 months or more forms a dull, slightly rough zinc patina. It gives a mechanical key for paint, so etching or a wash primer is usually not needed. Source: American Galvanizers Association, Duplex Systems (Painting Over Hot-Dip Galvanized Steel); ASTM D6386.

q: What is the process of preparing a surface by applying a base coat to improve paint adhesion, seal the substrate, and enhance the durability of the final coat?
n: Priming applies a base coat that seals the substrate, improves adhesion and evens out absorption for the topcoat. Source: ASTM D16 (Primer); PDCA Painting Standards.

q: AIPHONE is a known brand of what system?
n: Aiphone is a Japanese maker of intercom, door-entry and nurse-call systems, which are widely used in Philippine buildings. Source: Aiphone product catalog; NFPA 72 (Emergency Communication Systems).

q: Approximately how much water can a single waterless urinal save annually compared to a conventional flushing urinal?
n: Per the exam key, a waterless urinal can save on the order of 100,000 liters of water a year, depending on use. Source: US EPA WaterSense (Urinals); Philippine Green Building Code (2015), Water Efficiency.

q: In water closets, which of the following features typically does not make it more expensive?
n: Two-piece water closets, with the tank separate from the bowl, are the standard economical type. One-piece, skirted-trapway and wall-hung models cost more. Source: RSMeans Building Construction Cost Data (Plumbing Fixtures); manufacturers' price tiers.

q: What is the primary purpose of a wall chaser tool in construction?
o: Cutting grooves in walls for electrical wiring
n: A wall chaser has twin diamond blades that cut parallel grooves (chases) in masonry or concrete. Conduits and pipes are then embedded in the grooves. Source: Power-tool manufacturers' references; PEC Part 1, Art. 3 (concealed wiring in masonry).

q: In tools and equipment, what does the term grit primarily refer to?
o: The thickness of an abrasive material
The coarseness or fineness of an abrasive material
The durability of a cutting blade
The speed of a power tool
n: Grit is the size of the abrasive particles on sandpaper or a grinding disc. Low numbers are coarse and high numbers are fine. Source: ANSI B74.12 / FEPA grit standards.

q: In structural construction, where is the greatest bearing stress typically located?
n: The greatest bearing stress usually occurs between a beam and a girder because the beam transfers concentrated loads directly onto the girder, creating a high compressive force at the contact area. In contrast, connections like ridgeboard and rafter or column base and foundation distribute forces more evenly, reducing bearing stress. Per the exam key, the greatest bearing stress is taken to occur where a beam delivers a concentrated reaction onto a girder. Note: column base plates on footings are also critical bearing points. Source: NSCP 2015, Sec. 422.8 (Bearing); Gere & Goodno, Mechanics of Materials.

q: What are reentrant corners in building construction?
n: Reentrant corners occur where two perpendicular building sections meet, forming an inward notch. These corners can create stress concentration points and are susceptible to damage during seismic events. Reentrant corners are the inside corners where wings of an L-, T- or U-shaped plan meet. Seismic stresses concentrate there, and NSCP treats them as a plan irregularity. Source: NSCP 2015, Table 208-10 (Plan Structural Irregularities – Reentrant Corners).

q: Which building is known for its use of diagrid as structural elements?
n: The Hearst Tower in New York is renowned for its innovative use of diagrid structural elements, which consist of a diagonal grid pattern that reduces the need for vertical columns, making the structure both lighter and more efficient. Foster + Partners' Hearst Tower (2006) is famous for its triangulated diagrid, which saved about 20% of the steel. The Gherkin is also a diagrid. Source: CTBUH, Hearst Tower case study; Foster + Partners project data.

q: The natural angle and maximum practical angle for changing grades without using retaining walls or other stabilization techniques.
n: The angle of repose is the steepest natural slope at which a soil stands without retaining walls or other stabilization. Source: Das, Principles of Geotechnical Engineering; De Chiara & Koppelman, Time-Saver Standards for Site Planning (Grading).

q: What is the primary purpose of a development length in reinforced concrete construction?
o: To increase the compressive strength of concrete
To minimize thermal expansion of steel bars
To ensure adequate bond between steel and concrete
To reduce the overall weight of the structure
n: Development length is the embedment a bar needs so that bond with the concrete can develop its full design stress without slipping. Source: NSCP 2015, Sec. 425.4 (Development of Reinforcement); ACI 318.

q: Which wood coating is primarily used to seal the surface before applying the final finish, helping to fill pores and create a smooth base?
n: Sanding sealer is applied over bare wood before the topcoat. It seals and partly fills the pores, and once sanded it leaves a smooth, even base. Source: Fine Woodworking finishing references; Hoadley, Understanding Wood.

q: Gmelina is most commonly used for which application?
n: Gmelina (yemane) is a fast-growing plantation wood. It is light, easy to work and stable, so it is mainly used for furniture, cabinetry and light construction. Source: DENR-FPRDI, Philippine Woods (Gmelina arborea); FAO plantation species data.

q: What is Kamagong also commonly known as due to its exceptional hardness and density?
n: Per the exam key, kamagong's exceptional hardness and density earn it the name "ironwood" in common use. Source: DENR-FPRDI, Philippine Woods (Kamagong, Diospyros blancoi).

q: What is a common term used in the Philippine construction industry to describe lumber that has been sawn but not yet surfaced or dressed, often sold at a lower price point?
n: Rough lumber has been sawn but not planed or dressed (S4S). It is cheaper and used for forms and hidden framing. Source: Max Fajardo, Simplified Construction Estimate (Lumber); American Softwood Lumber Standard PS 20.

q: Which of the following construction woods is currently generally prohibited from logging in natural forests in the Philippines due to conservation concerns?
n: Narra, the national tree, is a threatened species. Cutting it from natural forests is prohibited under DENR rules and the logging moratorium. Source: EO 23 s.2011 (Moratorium on Logging in Natural Forests); DENR DAO 2017-11 (Threatened Plants).

q: Which structural component typically experiences the greatest overturning load during seismic or wind events?
n: A shear wall is specifically designed to resist lateral forces caused by wind or seismic events, which can produce significant overturning moments. These walls help maintain the stability of the structure by counteracting tipping forces. Foundations primarily bear vertical loads, columns support axial and bending forces, and beams primarily resist bending moments, but none are as directly involved in resisting overturning forces as shear walls. Shear walls carry a large share of the lateral force over their height, so overturning moment concentrates at their base. That governs their boundary elements and foundations. Source: NSCP 2015, Sec. 208 and Sec. 418.10 (Special Structural Walls).

q: Which testing method is used to evaluate the bearing capacity and integrity of piles by measuring their response to impact loads?
n: A Dynamic Pile Test measures the bearing capacity and integrity of piles by analyzing their response to impact loads, typically applied by a hammer or drop weight. The data collected helps assess pile strength, length, and soil resistance. In contrast, a Static Pile Test applies a gradual load, an Ultrasonic Pulse Velocity Test measures concrete quality, and a Load Bearing Capacity Test evaluates general support capacity without specifically analyzing dynamic responses. A dynamic pile test (Pile Driving Analyzer, high-strain test) strikes the pile with a hammer and measures force and velocity. From these it estimates capacity and integrity. Source: ASTM D4945 (High-Strain Dynamic Testing of Deep Foundations).

q: A steel beam in a high-rise building experiences deformation under a heavy load. Which material property, represented by Young's modulus, is primarily responsible for determining how much the beam will bend or stretch?
n: Young's modulus measures the elasticity of a material, indicating how much it will deform under | stress. A higher Young's modulus means the material is stiffer and will bend or stretch less when | subjected to a load. Ductility refers to stretchability without breaking, hardness indicates resistance to surface indentation, and toughness measures energy absorption before fracturing. In structural applications, elasticity is crucial for predicting beam deflection and ensuring structural stability. Young's modulus measures elasticity (stiffness): how much a member strains under stress within the elastic range, and so how much it deflects or stretches. Source: Gere & Goodno, Mechanics of Materials; NSCP 2015, Ch. 5 (E = 200 GPa).

q: What is the primary cause of deflection in a structural beam?
n: Beam deflection occurs primarily due to applied loads and bending moments, which cause the beam to deform or bend. The amount of deflection depends on factors like load intensity, span length, material stiffness (Young's modulus), and beam geometry. While thermal expansion can cause slight movement, corrosion weakens the material, and foundation settlement affects the overall | structure, they do not directly cause beam deflection as bending and applied loads do. Beams deflect under applied loads and the resulting bending moments. Deflection depends on load, span, stiffness (EI) and support conditions. Source: Gere & Goodno, Mechanics of Materials; NSCP 2015, Sec. 424.2 (Deflection).

q: Which property of structural elements allows them to undergo significant deformation before failure, making them resilient during seismic events?
n: Ductility lets members deform well beyond yield without collapsing. They absorb and dissipate seismic energy and give warning before failure. Source: NSCP 2015, Sec. 208 (ductility and R factors); Paulay & Priestley, Seismic Design of RC and Masonry Buildings.

q: What grade of stainless steel is commonly used in commercial grease trap?
n: Commercial grease traps are fabricated from Grade 304 stainless steel. It resists the corrosion of hot, greasy kitchen wastewater and is easy to clean. Source: Revised National Plumbing Code (Grease Interceptors); ASTM A240 (Grade 304).

q: In a typical grease trap, the first compartment from the inlet is composed of what component?
n: The inlet compartment of a grease trap usually has a removable filter (strainer) basket. It catches food solids before the wastewater reaches the separation chambers. Source: PDI-G101 (Grease Interceptors); Revised National Plumbing Code.

q: Spacing of cleanouts along a horizontal drainage pipe?
n: Horizontal drainage lines need cleanouts at most about 15 m (50 ft) apart, plus at changes of direction. Source: Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Sec. 707 (Cleanouts); Uniform Plumbing Code, Sec. 707.

q: What type of water heater is commonly used to provide hot water to both the kitchen and bathroom from a single unit?
n: A multipoint water heater is designed to supply hot water to multiple locations within a building, such as the kitchen and bathroom, from a single unit. Unlike instantaneous or tankless heaters, which typically serve a single point of use, multipoint heaters efficiently deliver hot water to several outlets. A multipoint water heater, usually instantaneous, has enough capacity to feed several outlets, such as kitchen sink and shower, from one unit. A single-point unit serves one outlet. Source: Stein & Reynolds, Mechanical and Electrical Equipment for Buildings (Water Heating).

q: Pipe slope is most critical in which type of plumbing pipe?
n: Drainage pipes work by gravity, so their slope (usually 1–2%) is critical for self-cleansing flow. Supply pipes are pressurized. Source: Revised National Plumbing Code, Sec. 708 (Grade of Horizontal Drainage Piping).

q: Which of the following materials is traditionally used as a base or surface to receive plasterwork on walls and ceilings?
n: Lath (wood strips, metal mesh or gypsum lath) is the traditional base that plaster is applied to and keys into on walls and ceilings. Source: Ching, Building Construction Illustrated, Ch. 10 (Plaster – Lath); ASTM C841/C847.

q: Which of the following describes a roof structure constructed using a network of intersecting diagonal ribs forming a diamond pattern, often resulting in a lightweight and strong shell?
n: A lamella roof is a vault of short, identical members (lamellas) intersecting diagonally in a diamond pattern. It makes a light, strong shell. Source: Ching, A Visual Dictionary of Architecture (Lamella Roof); Schodek & Bechthold, Structures.

q: A reinforced concrete beam having a depth to span ratio greater than 2.50.
n: Per the exam key, a deep beam is defined by its large depth relative to span. Code note: the NSCP defines deep beams by clear span ≤ 4 × depth. Source: NSCP 2015, Sec. 409.9 (Deep Beams); ACI 318.

q: In a typical reinforced concrete (RC) frame building, punching shear failure is most likely to occur where?
n: Punching shear occurs where a concentrated reaction is transferred through a slab. That makes the slab around columns, in flat plates and flat slabs, the critical zone. Source: NSCP 2015, Sec. 422.6 (Two-Way Shear); MacGregor & Wight, Reinforced Concrete.

q: Which of the following types of beams is specifically designed to receive the ends of joists or a slab along its side, often utilizing ledgers or other connection methods?
n: Per the exam key, the spandrel beam, the edge beam at the perimeter of a floor, receives the ends of joists or slab along its side, often through ledgers. Source: Ching, A Visual Dictionary of Architecture (Spandrel Beam); NSCP 2015, Ch. 4.

q: What does "PB" mean?
n: Per the exam key, on electrical plans "PB" is a pull box. Pull boxes are used where long or bent conduit runs need access for pulling wires. Source: Philippine Electrical Code 2017, Part 1, Art. 3.14 (Pull and Junction Boxes); IEEE 315 (Graphic Symbols).

q: What does FACP mean?
n: FACP means Fire Alarm Control Panel. It monitors the detectors and initiating devices and activates the notification appliances. Source: NFPA 72 (Fire Alarm and Signaling Code); RA 9514 RIRR.

q: What is the most common unit used to measure the concentration of carbon monoxide (CO) in air and indoor spaces?
n: ppm (parts per million) is the standard unit for measuring low concentrations of gases like carbon monoxide in air. It represents the number of CO molecules per million air molecules, making it suitable for the trace amounts typically found. Carbon monoxide concentration is usually expressed in parts per million (ppm). CO alarms and exposure limits are given in ppm. Source: UL 2034 (CO Alarms); WHO Indoor Air Quality Guidelines; DOLE OSHS Table of TLVs.

q: Which of the following brands is widely recognized and known for its Fire Detection and Alarm Systems (FDAS) in the Philippines and globally?
n: Honeywell, including its Notifier and Gent lines, is a globally known maker of fire detection and alarm systems. Source: Honeywell Fire Safety product catalog; NFPA 72 (Fire Alarm and Signaling Code).

q: In architectural lighting, which of the following angles is typically the widest when describing the spread of light from a fixture?
n: The field angle is the widest angle in lighting design, representing the area where the light intensity drops to 10% of the maximum. It encompasses the full spread of light emitted from the fixture. In contrast, the beam angle represents the more concentrated central beam (50% of maximum intensity), the cutoff angle limits the point where light is no longer emitted, and focus angle is not a standard lighting term. The field angle, measured to 10% of peak intensity, is wider than the beam angle, measured to 50%. It describes the full spread of the light. Source: IES Lighting Handbook, 10th ed. (Beam and Field Angles).

q: What is the primary purpose of a photometric curve in architectural lighting?
o: To measure the color temperature of a light source
To calculate the power consumption of a lighting system
To represent the distribution of light intensity from a fixture
To determine the electrical efficiency of a lighting fixture
n: A photometric curve (candela distribution or polar curve) shows how a luminaire's light intensity is distributed by direction. Source: IES Lighting Handbook (Photometric Data); IES LM-63.

q: On average, how much energy can be saved by using LED lighting compared with traditional incandescent bulbs?
n: LED lamps use about 75–80% less energy than incandescent lamps for the same light output. Source: US Department of Energy, LED Lighting; Philippine DOE, Lighting Efficiency programs.

q: In lighting systems, LLF is a factor used to account for the reduction in light output over time due to factors like dirt accumulation, lamp depreciation, and fixture degradation. What does LLF stand for?
n: LLF means Light Loss Factor. It combines lamp lumen depreciation, luminaire dirt depreciation and similar losses in lighting calculations. Source: IES Lighting Handbook (Light Loss Factors).

q: Which of the following situations is most likely to cause a veiling reflection in an interior space?
o: Bright light reflecting off a glossy tabletop
Indirect lighting from a cove light
Diffused lighting from a frosted glass fixture
Soft ambient light from recessed fixtures
n: Veiling reflections are images of bright sources reflected off glossy task surfaces such as tables and screens. They wash out contrast. Source: IES Lighting Handbook (Veiling Reflections); Lechner, Heating, Cooling, Lighting.
